title: Sub-millimeter sized multi-component jet fuel surrogate droplet combustion: Physicochemical preferential vaporization effects (2021)
summary: Proc. Combust. Inst. 38 (2021): 1-D spherically symmetric simulations of droplets of three Jet-A surrogate mixtures with very different distillation curves. Mixture-1 predictions agree with drop-tower data for 550 um droplets in air when near-full internal mixing and sooting are included. Preferential vaporization depends non-linearly on droplet size and pressure: frozen-limit vaporization at low pressure and small sizes, batch distillation at practical pressures.

items.claim: Preferential vaporization of multicomponent jet-fuel surrogate droplets depends strongly and non-linearly on initial diameter and pressure; frozen-limit vaporization at low pressure/small drops, batch distillation at application pressures.
items.quote: By comparing predictions for the three mixtures, preferential vaporization effects exhibit strong non-linear dependences on initial droplet diameter and ambient pressure.

items.claim: Model validated against drop-tower 550 um droplet data (not ISS).
items.quote: The predictions using Mixture-1 are found to be in good agreement with previously published drop-tower experiments for 550 µm droplet combustion in air.

notes: Abstract via OpenAlex; ScienceDirect accepted manuscript returned HTTP 403. Validation is against drop-tower, not FLEX, data.

title: Initial diameter effects on combustion of unsupported equi-volume n-heptane/iso-octane mixture droplets and the transition to cool flame behavior: Experimental observations and detailed numerical modeling (2020)
summary: Combustion and Flame 2020: experiments and detailed modelling of unsupported equi-volume n-heptane/iso-octane mixture droplets over a range of initial diameters from 0.8 mm upward, and the transition to cool-flame behaviour. The available abstract is truncated after the diameter range, so no results could be extracted.
notes: Abstract truncated at the source (OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar stop at '0.8 mm ≤ Do'); Elsevier full text paywalled. Topic (mixture droplets, diameter effect on cool-flame transition) is not covered by the PSI-117 record; not added for lack of results.

title: Oscillatory cool flame combustion behavior of submillimeter sized n-alkane droplet under near limit conditions (2019)
summary: Proc. Combust. Inst. 37 (2019): simulated oscillatory cool-flame burning of sub-millimetre n-heptane droplets with ozone seeding at 1 atm. At 21% O2 a quasi-steady cool flame forms directly; at low O2 with 5% O3 a cool flame forms then oscillates with growing amplitude until burnout, driven by fuel-vapour depletion and re-establishment and by fuel and oxygen leakage through the flame.

items.claim: Direct cool-flame burning with O3 seeding at 21% O2.
items.quote: For XO2= 21% and a range of selective ozone seeding, near-quasi-steady cool flame burning is achieved directly (without requiring hot flame initiation and radiative extinction).

items.claim: Oscillating cool flame at low O2 with 5% O3, growing amplitude, fuel/oxygen leakage.
items.quote: Under low oxygen index conditions, but with significant O3 seeding (XO3 = 5%), a nearly quasi-steady cool flame is initially established that then transitions to a dynamically oscillating cool flame burning mode which continues until the droplet is completely consumed.

notes: Abstract via OpenAlex; accepted manuscript returned HTTP 403. The PSI presentation 'PSI-117_Presentations_Oscillatory_Cool Flame_TFarouk.pdf' covers the same work.
